rules: 723.1. Some cards allow a player to control another player during that player’s next turn. This effect applies to the next turn that the affected player actually takes. The affected player is controlled during the entire turn; the effect doesn’t end until the beginning of the next turn.
723.1a Multiple player-controlling effects that affect the same player overwrite each other. The last one to be created is the one that works.
723.1b If a turn is skipped, any pending player-controlling effects wait until the player who would be affected actually takes a turn.

800.4b If an object would change to the control of a player who has left the game, it doesn’t. If a token would be created under the control of a player who has left the game, no token is created. If an object would be put onto the battlefield or onto the stack under the control of a player who has left the game, that object remains in its current zone. If a player would be controlled by a player who has left the game, they aren’t.
versioned_rules_reference.limit: Retained versioned reference, not a complete current-rules audit

limits: Controlled partial four-player boards. Both native stack-copy modes are checked at resolved checkpoints; no arbitrary paid pending spells or mid-resolution continuations are certified.

Twenty-two paid lifecycle cases across both modes, four controller-layer/factory-history contracts, two concession diagnostic controls and two expired positive controls comprise the thirty native cases.

Thirteen packaged witnesses preserve actual costs, active/lost players, master/view/registered-agent identity, independent game-bound controller objects, phases, extra-turn flags and card zones or explicit absence.

Registered controller factories are restored without new control events. Arbitrary custom factories outside registered participants are rejected explicitly; custom strategy state and human-controller conversion remain unverified.

Secret of Bloodbending uses its normal four-blue cost without optional waterbend payment. Emrakul uses thirteen mana, no graveyard reduction and its native mandatory trigger target; the promised uncontrolled extra turn is checked.
Other control cards, skipped turns, active-master departure, targets leaving, search-only control, response priority, optional cost variants and hostile decision policy remain unverified.

Native action admission/payment do not establish automated selection. A separate source-bound probe reproduces unsupported CantPlayAi decisions for three legal, affordable actions without requiring selection of every legal action.
Unmapped callbacks are asserted in fixtures, not yet aggregated into regular CLI reports. Other callbacks, hidden/merged/perpetual state and arbitrary suspended continuations remain open.

Catalog construction proves script availability rather than full gameplay correctness. Seven unavailable entries are nonstarting meld results. Versioned references are not a complete current-rules audit.
